findings.title: `{...props}` in `PasswordField` overrides `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` when caller passes `type="password"`
findings.body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (line 176), `<TextField type="password" ... />` was replaced with `<PasswordField type="password" ... />`. However, inside `PasswordField` (`packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx`), `{...props}` is spread after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}`. Because `EnableTwoFactorModal` explicitly passes `type="password"`, that prop overwrites the computed `type`, so clicking the show/hide password eye toggle button in the Enable 2FA modal has no effect and the password always remains hidden. Either remove `type="password"` in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` or spread `{...props}` before `type` in `PasswordField`.

findings.title: Third-party IdP 2FA login (`?totp=`) cannot use backup codes
findings.body: In `authorize`, lines 114, 118, and 122 only skip the `IdentityProvider.CAL` and password checks when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`), not when `credentials.backupCode` is provided. Also, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (line 180), when `totpEmail` is set (the OAuth/SAML 2FA flow via `/auth/login?totp=...`), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, which hides the "Lost access" button altogether, and even if a backup code were submitted, `authorize` would reject the login with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` because `credentials.totpCode` is empty. Users who log in via Google or SAML with 2FA enabled are therefore unable to use backup codes.

findings.title: `expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes a Promise to `expect()` without awaiting it, and the first test never closes the backup codes step
findings.body: In the first e2e test (`should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA`), after `fillOtp` enables 2FA, the modal transitions to the new `DisplayBackupCodes` step and stays open (because `onEnable` is now only called when clicking `backup-codes-close`). The test does not click `backup-codes-close`, and as noted by the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` only passes because `isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>`, and a Promise object is always truthy in synchronous `.toBeTruthy()`—the switch is actually still unchecked in the UI (`onEnable` was never invoked). The test should click `backup-codes-close` and use `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]')).toBeChecked()` (or check `data-state="checked"`).
